name: Columbia Valley
terms: American Viticultural Area. A wine labeled with one must take at least 85% of its grapes from that area.
keyfacts: Columbia Valley is a large AVA covering much of central and southern Washington and reaching into northern Oregon, established in 1984.

Over 99% of Washington's vineyard acreage lies within it, and almost all the state's growing regions, including Walla Walla Valley, Yakima Valley, Red Mountain and Horse Heaven Hills, are sub-appellations of it.
The Cascade Range casts a rain shadow, leaving an average of 6 to 8 inches of rain a year, so vineyards depend on irrigation.
Irrigation water comes from the Columbia River and its tributaries, along with aquifers.

notes: Warm days and cool nights keep acid and sugar in balance, and the long season lets tannins mature.

blurb.text: A huge AVA covering much of central and southern Washington and crossing into northern Oregon, across the Columbia River Plateau. It contains Walla Walla Valley, Yakima Valley, Red Mountain and Horse Heaven Hills.
